stories.title: President House says matters related to provinces did not come under discussion during Zardari, Naqvi meeting
summary: The President House said on Friday refuted media reports about yesterday’s meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, saying that discussions focused on national security and regional situation.
The clarification comes after several media reports emerged claiming that Naqvi and the president had discussed the formation of new provinces during a meeting in Nawabshah on Thursday night.

Meanwhile, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has called for a “full stop” on the debate surrounding new provinces and also a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”.

stories.title: US Treasury chief blames Commerce Dept for failure in Nvidia scandal
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday blamed the Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the centre of a scandal that prompted Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to resign.
Megaspeed is suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls by buying Nvidia chips for its data centres in Southeast Asia and routing them to China.
Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in a November 8 letter to Nvidia employees that did not name the woman involved and resigned his position on Thursday.

stories.title: Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes
summary: Old-school technology including telephones, faxes and Bluetooth limited the damage for some people on Friday as a worldwide outage of Microsoft’s Outlook left millions without email.
Microsoft, which says on its website that more than 430 million people use its 365 services, blamed server problems and said it was not aware of any malicious activity.
Fax machines return in Taipei In Taiwan, the outage disrupted fund management at securities firms, life insurers and investment trust companies, people familiar with the situation said.

stories.title: Barrick Mining expresses interest in mineral processing industries in Karachi, Gwadar
summary: It added that the prime minister also expressed a desire to draw on Barrick’s expertise and experience to develop Pakistan’s mineral sector beyond Reko Diq.

Furthermore, per the statement, the PM said the exchange of MoUs at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum was a “welcome” development. “Creating a conducive environment for investment in the minerals sector is among the government’s priorities.

stories.title: COP has a guest-list problem
summary: Moved by her experience, Jamali decided to apply for participation in the 27th edition of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) COP, scheduled to be held in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt in November that year.

Durlabh Ashok, founding director of Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), a leading youth-led climate organisation that sends delegations to COP every year, says the organisation offers limited financial assistance to its delegates.
He was selected to attend COP30 through Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), however, he was required to submit $2,200 (approximately PKR 620,448 at the time) for the trip.

stories.title: Nvidia fallout throws spotlight on Southeast Asia’s AI boom
summary: Southeast Asia’s chip and data centre industries expect greater scrutiny after news of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy put the spotlight on Singapore and Malaysia, executives and analysts said.

The alleged spy, Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, was an executive at a cloud computing firm in Singapore called Megaspeed that has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.

Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data centre consultancy Sprint DC, likened the current situation to a “post-DeepSeek moment”. “Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia.

stories.title: Microsoft says ‘improvements’ for Outlook in North America, Europe
summary: Microsoft said on Friday that it was seeing “improvements” for Outlook email and other services amid an outage that was disrupting public services and businesses around the world.

In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organisations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft does not suspect a cyber attack. “The impact that they are dealing with … is very much on email systems,” the minister added.
Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted the tech giant’s suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide.

stories.title: Pakistan aiming to become competitive destination for long-term investment, CDF Munir tells minerals moot
summary: As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.
PM expresses hope for Pakistan’s economy Addressing the same event, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed the hope that Pakistan could become the world’s sixth-largest economy “earlier than 2050”.

Regarding Pakistan’s efforts to meet investor expectations, PM Shehbaz highlighted that the country was simplifying procedures, “eliminating red tape, cutting inordinate delays and ensuring complete transparency in awarding licences and contracts”.

stories.title: ECP gives federal govt 2 weeks to submit formal request for cantonment board polls
summary: Previously, the ECP said delimitation in all cantonments had been completed, but it was awaiting formal request and response from the Ministry of Defence, to which it had written several letters and also sent a letter to the prime minister without response.
The commission had directed the defence ministry to initiate a summary for obtaining the federal government’s request and forward it to the ECP.

At Tuesday’s hearing, Brigadier (retired) Falak Naz, who is the legal adviser to the defence ministry, and Additional Director General of ML&CD Khalil Ahmad Rana told the commission that the ministry was ready to hold the elections, but the matter remained pending with the PMO.

stories.title: Pakistan, bad weather hold Sri Lanka to draw in first Test
summary: Led by Saud Shakeel and aided by bad weather, Pakistan foiled Sri Lanka’s bid for victory as the first Test ended in a draw on the fifth and final day in Rawalpindi on Friday.
Sri Lanka had sniffed victory with four wickets in the first session, with Pakistan 151-5 at lunch and a lead of 139.
Earlier, Sri Lanka struck with the first ball of the day when Kumara dismissed Azan Awais for 22 at Pakistan’s overnight total of 57.

stories.title: North Korean hackers stole $400m using fake video calls: FBI
summary: North Korea’s state-backed hackers stole more than $400 million using a “highly effective social engineering scheme” involving identity theft and AI-powered fake video calls, the FBI said on Thursday.
The FBI said that, aside from the Binance hack, North Koreans have “aggressively [targeted] individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors through deceptive social engineering tactics”.
FaceStealer hackers pretend to be someone known to the victim to lure them to a video meeting, using AI-powered deepfake video to gain trust.

stories.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 11.21pc
summary: Short-term inflation has remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum and diesel prices.
The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly declined by 0.46pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items.

The items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included tomatoes (12.06pc), eggs (5.98pc), potatoes (2.42pc), garlic (1.76pc), chicken (1.32pc), firewood (1.10pc), wheat flour (0.94pc), pulse masoor (0.64pc), beef (0.47pc), and LPG (0.30pc).

stories.title: Islamabad to become country's first fully cashless city by year-end
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has decided to make the federal capital the country’s first fully cashless city, setting Dec 31 as the deadline for the transition.

The decision was taken at an important meeting on the Cashless Capital project chaired by State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudry, in Islamabad on Friday, according to an official statement by the Ministry of Interior on X.
Representatives of the banking sector appreciated the government’s Cashless Islamabad initiative and assured full cooperation for its success, it added.

stories.title: Copper, gold deposits identified at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district: mining company
summary: ISLAMABAD: Mining company National Resources Limited (NRL) on Friday announced that it had identified copper and gold deposits at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district, following nearly 25,000 metres of drilling that yielded encouraging results.

Tabba reaffirmed NRL’s previously announced commitment of $100 million to mineral exploration in Pakistan and invited domestic and international investors and service providers to explore emerging opportunities.
The company’s technical workforce is almost entirely local, supporting its ambition to build domestic expertise that could also contribute to international exploration projects.

stories.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted major city as air quality deteriorates
summary: India’s capital, Delhi, overtook Lahore to become the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with air quality reaching hazardous levels and visibility dropping as smog blanketed the city of 20 million people.

Earlier, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 334, categorised as “hazardous”, making it the most polluted major city globally, according to Swiss air quality monitoring group IQAir, which measures pollution levels based on the concentration of pollutants.

The spokesperson said comparative data for the period between Jan 1 and Nov 10 this year showed a “substantial increase” in inspections, regulatory action and financial penalties against polluting industries and brick kilns compared to the corresponding period last year.

stories.title: India blocks over 100 speakers from opposition democracy summit
summary: Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and former senior United Nations official, said 115 of the 315 speakers cleared by India’s foreign ministry were subsequently refused entry or had their visas cancelled, “apparently on the instructions” of the home ministry.
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng said on Wednesday that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to travel to India, where she had been invited to speak on media and press freedom.
Today the Association of Norwegian Editors and the Norwegian Press Association have sent an open letter to the Embassy of India in Oslo, Norway.

stories.title: Vehicle emission testing: A step-by-step guide for Punjab's motorists
summary: Step 2: Visit an authorised emission-testing centre Vehicle owners are required to take their vehicles to an authorised testing centre with the necessary documentation.
The Punjab government has established 28 vehicle emission-testing centres in Lahore under a public-private partnership model.
Keep in mind The Punjab government had initially set Oct 15 as the deadline for vehicle emission testing.

stories.title: Henry takes six as New Zealand thrash India by 244 runs
summary: Matt Henry took six wickets and Will Young struck a century as New Zealand thrashed a ragged India by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Mount Maunganui on Friday.
New Zealand’s imposing total came off the back of Young’s 125 from 108 balls, including 14 fours and four sixes.

stories.title: Asean faces Myanmar dilemma as some members pursue closer ties
summary: Asean is under increasing pressure at its upcoming summit to ease a five-year ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending high-level meetings, after Thailand and several other members stepped up engagement despite the country’s ongoing civil war.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, Asean’s special envoy, visited Myanmar on a humanitarian mission in October.

Testing Asean unity Thailand’s assertive engagement reflects the country’s concerns over fighting spilling across its long land border with Myanmar, alongside trade, migrant workers and energy cooperation.

stories.title: UN envoy urges Australia to act on 'embarrassing' Indigenous rights record
summary: Australia must take urgent action to protect Indigenous peoples’ rights, a United Nations expert warned, describing the country’s record as “embarrassing” and damaging to its international reputation, according to local broadcaster ABC on Friday.

Albert Barume, the UN special rapporteur on the rights of Indigenous peoples, made the remarks after a two-week visit to Australia, during which he was denied access to youth detention centers in Queensland and the Northern Territory.
"I'm convinced Indigenous peoples' rights … are unsafe in the hands of states and territories," Barume told reporters in Sydney.

stories.title: Manchester United name Pochettino as new manager
summary: Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager on Friday following the dismissal of Michael Carrick.
The club issued a statement saying the USA coach, who has extensive experience in the Premier League, would take charge from November 18 following two matches against Haiti.

"The club has reached an agreement with the US soccer federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men's national team," United said.

stories.title: SpaceX to attempt first Starship spacecraft recovery on land in 15th flight
summary: SpaceX's latest Starship flight planned for Friday will include its first attempt to ​catch the spacecraft at its Texas launch site rather than discarding it in the ocean, a key test of Elon Musk’s bid to ‌make a fully reusable rocket system.

The 407-foot-tall (124 m) Starship rocket is scheduled to launch at 4:45 p.m. CT (2245 GMT) from SpaceX's Starbase launch facilities in South Texas for its 15th flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites.

NASA has helped fund Starship's development with roughly $3.2 billion delivered ​to SpaceX since selecting the rocket in 2021 to serve as a moon lander for its astronauts under the ​multibillion-dollar US Artemis moon ⁠program.

stories.title: SC rules inheritance rights do not expire with time
summary: The court clarified that the limitation period for filing an inheritance claim begins only when the heir is made aware of a clear denial of their ownership rights.

In a detailed judgement, a five-member bench held that no court could presume that the limitation period had commenced unless an heir had been informed of an unequivocal act denying their inheritance rights.
The court held that a limitation defence could prevent an heir from pursuing a claim if they remained inactive for six years after being informed of an unequivocal denial of their inheritance rights.

stories.title: Russell Brand faces fresh accusations as six more women speak out after prison sentence
summary: Russell Brand is facing fresh allegations of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour after six more women came forward with accounts of their experiences involving the comedian, days after his conviction for rape and sexual assault.

An investigation by The Times and The Sunday Times, published on November 12, detailed allegations from women who described encounters they said involved unwanted sexual behaviour, intimidation and abuse of Brand’s celebrity status.
The latest accounts come after Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on November 9.

stories.title: New allegations adds third woman to Jensen Huang’s growing scandal hours after he resigned
summary: Jensen Huang is facing fresh scrutiny over his personal life after a new report alleged that the former Nvidia chief executive had an intimate relationship with another company employee, adding to the growing controversy surrounding his reported extramarital affairs.
According to Reuters, published on November 12, two people familiar with the matter said Huang had been involved with a second Nvidia employee.
One involved Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, whose alleged affair with Huang was reported by The New York Times on November 11.

stories.title: 35 more electric buses arrive in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: As many as 35 more electric buses arrived in the garrison city which increased the total strength of the fleet to 80.

summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Railways and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) are at loggerheads over the ownership of a piece of land worth billions of rupees and construction of a godown and warehouses in Sector I-9.
The CDA board headed by its chairman Sohail Ashraf on Thursday heard Pakistan Railways (PR) officials over railways auction of land in I-9, which CDA says is part of the right of way.

The court also stated: “In view of foregoing discussion, this Court is unable to accept petitioners’ principal contention that CDA is wholly without jurisdiction to regulate construction on the subject land.

summary: Several pro-Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) accounts and some media outlets shared a video on Thursday across social media platforms that allegedly showed PTI founder Imran Khan’s sisters Noreen and Uzma Khanum after their release from Kot Lakhpat jail.

stories.title: Russia demands Finland leave NATO in Abu Dhabi talks: report
summary: Russian negotiators have put forward far-reaching demands during Abu Dhabi talks to end the war in Ukraine, including Finland leaving NATO and a ban on any NATO military bases in the Baltic states, the German newspaper Bild reported on Friday.

Read: Putin lets Europe join Ukraine peace talks, as Kyiv says Starshield disrupted again The daily said the proposal also calls for Ukraine to remain permanently non-aligned, ruling out NATO membership while leaving open the possibility of joining the European Union.
It further seeks a ban on NATO military bases in the Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, with Finland required to return to its pre-membership status.

summary: Judge Mohammad Zafar pronounced that the suspect, Musharraf Shah, a former cashier at National Bank of Pakistan, Dassu branch, was discharged from his liability as he had voluntarily surrendered the crime proceed.
The plea bargain application of the suspect was accepted by NAB chairman on Nov 4, 2026, and the matter was referred to the accountability court for final approval.

The special prosecutors of NAB, Habibullah Baig and Fahim Khan, along with the investigation officer Inayatullah Khan, appeared before the court and stated that the suspect had served as cashier in NBP Dassu branch from Oct 7, 2021, to March 5, 2025.

stories.title: Sindh CM calls for accelerated completion of climate-resilient projects
summary: KARACHI: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Thursday directed the provincial departments to speed up water security and climate-resilient projects.

The chief minister directed the irrigation department to maintain the improved flood-protection infrastructure, expedite ongoing drainage schemes and ensure efficient use of available water resources.

The chief minister said that the provincial government would continue to place communities at the centre of its climate-resilience strategy, ensuring that development initiatives deliver lasting improvements in people’s lives.

stories.title: Joint investigation team seizes pistol of Mir Raza’s business partner
summary: KARACHI: The Joint Investigation Team (JIT), formed by the Sindh government, to probe the mysterious death of a young businessman, Mir Raza Ali, has seized the licensed pistol of his partner.
Without naming the partner, West DIG Irfan Baloch, who heads the JIT, said on Thursday that the North Nazimabad branch of Mir Raza’s food chain has also been sealed for further investigation.
The JIT was formed on the recommendation of the judicial commission headed by a Sindh High Court judge to probe the alleged murder of Mir Raza.

stories.title: Lahore High Court moved against change of names of universities
summary: LAHORE: A petition has been filed in the Lahore High Court, challenging the removal of the word “university” from the names of six public sector varsities and demanding restoration of their former title of “college”.

The petition contends that the amendment arbitrarily downgraded the nomenclature of the institutions without consulting the stakeholders, including vice chancellors, faculty members, academic bodies and students.

It claims the change could also create complications for the graduates seeking employment, higher education and immigration-related credential verification abroad, as their degrees and academic records carry the previous university names.

stories.title: IHC suspends Islamabad local govt election schedule
summary: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday suspended the Election Commission of Pakistan's (ECP) schedule for local government elections in the federal capital, which were scheduled for December 20, and sought responses from the commission and other respondents by November 26.
In December 2025, the ECP issued an election schedule for Islamabad's local government polls, fixing February 15, 2026, as the polling date.
At the October 21 hearing, the ECP decided to hold the elections under the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act 2015, which had become effective again after the ordinance lapsed.

stories.title: New copper-gold deposits discovered in Balochistan's Chagai
summary: Mari Energies Limited announced a significant copper-gold discovery in Balochistan's Chagai district, approximately 50 kilometres east of the Reko Diq mining project, according to a statement submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Friday.

According to the statement, the energy company had completed approximately 25,000 metres of exploration drilling in two phases, Phase 1A and Phase 1B, with all drill holes reaching a depth of 500 metres.
The statement said drilling had identified copper mineralisation beneath approximately 100 metres of sediment, extending across an area of about 1.4 square kilometres.

stories.title: Two arrested after pet lioness kills farmhouse worker in Lahore's Kahna
summary: LAHORE: A farmhouse owner and a TikToker were arrested on Thursday after a 19-year-old farmhouse employee was killed by a pet lioness in the farmhouse in the Kahna area on Thursday.
A spokesperson for the office of the deputy inspector general (DIG) of police identified the arrested suspects as farmhouse owner Fayyaz and TikToker Nauman.
The spokesperson said Nauman had visited the farmhouse to make a TikTok video when the lioness allegedly went out of control and attacked Talha, a farm employee, leaving him critically injured.
